title: Buying Second Hand Sarees Online: What to Check Before You Pay
description: A practical checklist for buying preloved and second hand sarees online, covering condition, zari, measurements, photographs and returns.

body.text: Check five things before you buy any saree you cannot touch. What the fibre is and how the seller knows. The condition of the fold lines, pallu and borders. Whether the zari is real metal. The full measurements including whether a blouse piece is included. And what happens if it arrives and it is not as described.
A seller who answers all five without hesitating is one to buy from.
Why should you ask about the fibre first?
Every other consideration depends on it. Pure silk, art silk and polyester are different products at different prices, and photographs cannot tell them apart.

Ask directly. What fibre is this and how do you know. Acceptable answers include a Silk Mark tag, testing, or a description of how it was assessed. An unacceptable answer is silence, or the word silk repeated back to you. Our guide on [how to identify a pure silk saree](/journal/how-to-identify-pure-silk-saree) explains what to look for.
Which photographs should you ask for?
Most of what you need is visible if you know where to look.
**Ask for the reverse.** Handwoven silk shows small irregularities and the pattern is usually visible on the back. A reverse that is blank and perfectly flat suggests a power loom and synthetic yarn.
**Ask for a photograph along the folds.** This is where old silk fails first. Soft fold marks are ordinary. A pale line along a fold means the fibres are stressed and may split.

**Ask for a close view of the zari.** Pure zari darkens slowly and evenly as it ages, which is expected. Patchy darkening often means tested zari, which is worth knowing before you agree a price. Flaking, or thread coming away from the weave, is damage.
**Ask for the pallu and the border ends.** These get the most handling and show wear before anywhere else.
Photographs taken in daylight against a plain background tell you far more than styled ones. A seller who only offers styled images is showing you a mood.
Why is an honest condition description a good sign?

A listing that mentions a small stain, a pulled thread or a repair is more trustworthy than one that mentions nothing at all. Sarees that have been worn have histories. A seller willing to write the flaws down is a seller who does not expect to be argued with later.
Be specific in what you ask. Are there stains, are there tears or thin patches, has anything been repaired, is there any odour.
What measurements should you check?
Ask for the length and the width, and ask whether a blouse piece is included and whether it is attached or separate. Ask whether a fall and a pico edging have been done.
Saree lengths vary more than people expect, and a shorter one drapes differently. This is a simple question that avoids a real disappointment.

body.text: Why should you decide quickly on a preloved saree?
This is particular to preloved. There is one of each piece. It is not being restocked, and there is no second one in another colour.

If you are deciding between two sarees, decide quickly or accept that one of them will go. That is uncomfortable next to ordinary online shopping, and it is simply how a market of single pieces works. For the difference between preloved, pre owned and second hand, see [what preloved means](/journal/preloved-sarees-meaning).
How should you pay, and what about returns?
Pay through the site, not by direct transfer to a personal account. Read what the seller says about returns before you buy, not after.

Understand that a genuine return policy on one of a kind pieces usually covers arriving damaged or being significantly different from the description. It does not usually cover changing your mind, and that is reasonable when nothing can be resold as new stock.
The checklist, in short
Fibre confirmed and how. Condition stated honestly. Zari identified. Measurements given. Blouse piece clarified. Reverse and fold photographs seen. Returns understood. Payment through the site.
Eight questions. Ten minutes. It is the difference between a saree you love and a parcel you regret opening.
